newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Volatility trades struck in FTSE index.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Volatility trades struck in FTSE index.

text.p: The main equity options trades on Monday concerned positions in FTSE 100 index options against FTSE futures in volatility trades, dealers said.
If correctly hedged, these trades will make money irrespective of the market's direction and rely on volatility to increase/decrease depending on whether options were bought/sold.

The biggest deal was a bullish call spread which was hedged by selling futures. It consisted of buying 3,000 February 4350 calls and selling 3,000 February 4375 calls for a net debit of 10p against selling March FTSE futures at 4312.
By 1430 GMT, March futures were up 15 at 4314.
Over in stock options British Gas was fairly active. The biggest deal was a short strangle established by selling 500 June 220 puts at 9p as well as 500 June 260 puts at 12p.
The maximum profit of 21p will be made at expiry if the underlying shares stay between 220p and 260p. British Gas shares added 2p to 245-1/2p.
In pharmaceuticals group Glaxo Wellcome a long strangle was created through the purchase of 1,000 April 950 puts at 20p along with 1,000 April 1050 calls at 16p.
If the shares stay between 950p-1050p at expiry then both options will be worthless and a loss of 36p will be made.
For a profit, the shares need to be either below 914p or above 1086p.
In National Westminster Bank the main deal was a short straddle achieved by selling 500 April 800 puts and calls at 28p and 42p each.
NatWest shares went up 26-1/2p to 842-1/2p. The bank will announce its full year results on February 25.
